goal: Replace the ad-hoc per-screen useState/useEffect/runtime.send balance and activity fetching (duplicated in SendView.tsx and MainScreenView.tsx) with @tanstack/react-query, giving the wallet one shared, cached, invalidatable source of truth for token balances and the activity feed, plus balance-aware send validation.
outcome: A QueryClientProvider wraps the popup shell; useBalances(address) and useActivity(address) hooks (wrapping the existing runtime.send({type: "getBalance"|"getTokenBalances"|"getActivity"}) calls as queryFns) replace the local state in both SendView and MainScreenView. A successful send/receive mutation invalidates the relevant balance and activity query keys so both screens reflect the new balance without a manual reload. The send flow validates the entered amount against the live cached balance before allowing submission, surfacing an inline error rather than letting an insufficient-balance send reach the backend.

requirements.statement: No change to the transport layer (runtime.send, ProtocolMap) -- TanStack Query wraps the existing message-passing calls as queryFns/mutationFns; it does not replace them.
Query keys are keyed by [wallet.address, 'balances'] / [wallet.address, 'activity'] so multiple wallets don't collide in cache.
SendView.tsx's and MainScreenView.tsx's existing local useState balance-fetching blocks (e.g. SendView.tsx's TokenPickerStep load/useEffect block) are removed, not left alongside the new hooks.
Opening Send and Main Screen shows the same balance without duplicate independent fetches racing each other.
After a successful send, both Send and Main Screen reflect the updated balance without a manual popup reopen.
Attempting to send more than the current balance is blocked client-side with a clear inline message, validated against the query cache's current value.
The activity feed (packages/core/src/activity) is fetched via useQuery and invalidated on send/receive the same way balances are.
